description:
We are a team of sixth-form students at Watford Grammar School for Boys, looking to apply our physics and coding skills to real world problems. We aim to develop an immersive game that simulates real astronaut missions using physics-based modelling systems, allowing missions to be tested and explored in virtual environments.

We are particularly looking for teammates with experience or an interest in 3D game development, Unity or Unreal Engine, 3D modelling, game design, and physics modeling.

details:
Project Cronus is a space mission game and flight simulation system built to simulate real-world conditions and their effects on launch sequences alongside engineering decisions.

Our programme takes real-life models directly from NASA and their past missions to run a 100-trial Monte Carlo dispersion model, showing success rates of launch systems and live statuses of spaceship models across flight zones. Players can do a variety of things from choosing real engines to structural alloys, heat shields, propellant mass, and launch angles—or fly historical missions under strict budget caps while reacting to live weather rules and mid-flight anomalies.

This makes our project extremely important: after all, using real NASA equations for atmospheric, propulsion, weather-commit, and reentry heating physics allows students to interpret real-world impacts that cannot be visualised in classrooms. It gives students a clear visual idea of how each physical and material factor affects every launch decision they take.

What makes Project Cronus creative is turning aerospace equations and physics into a game where real-time mission control consoles are available, where every slider changes the rocket's physical appearance, exhaust, and survival odds on screen. We built the web application using React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and HTML5 Canvas, developed with AI eing used as assistance to help develop the UI rapidly in time for submissions while the team handled compiling our physics dossier, UI/Site map, testing and correspondencies within functions of the programme.

As a first prototype the UI is not entirely finished as the main focus was research, physics implementation and launch stage testing. Later models may involve expanding maps to simulate space exploration alongside launch patterns.
